subject: Geo-fallback SLA: request for standby-region RTO/RPO exception
messages:
From: Eliot Turner <eliot.turner@orchard-finance.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orchard Finance Procurement <procurement@orchard-finance.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo-fallback SLA: request for standby-region RTO/RPO exception

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Orchard's infra team is reviewing Redwoods' failover approach ahead of our security committee meeting. A quick question from our side: during the seasonal data migration (mid-November window) we expect a temporary throttling of the east-coast standby region. That could extend automated failover timelines.

Can Redwood provide an exception to the default multi-region RTO/RPO commitments for that maintenance window? Specifically, we need a written acknowledgement that Orchard can operate with a relaxed RTO of up to 4 hours and an RPO of up to 2 hours for the standby region on the migration day, with compensating controls (read-only fallback, backup snapshots every 30 minutes). We want this in writing for our audit packet.

Appreciate a short confirmation or a proposed mitigation by EOD Friday so we can include it in the packet.

Thanks,
Eliot Turner
Director, Infrastructure
Orchard Finance

Attachments: orchard_sla_appendix.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Eliot Turner <eliot.turner@orchard-finance.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo-fallback SLA: request for standby-region RTO/RPO exception

Hi Eliot — thanks for the clear ask and the appendix. Short answer: we can support a scoped exception for the declared maintenance window but we need to align internally on the operational mitigations and a narrow timebox.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to confirm a formal, time-limited SLA amendment that documents RTO=up to 4 hours / RPO=up to 2 hours for the standby region on the agreed migration date.
- Redwood CS/Runbooks team will provide a pre-migration checklist (KV cache warmup, pre-primed failover routing) and a 24-hour on-call commitment for that window.
- We will include a fallback plan to route critical customers to a third-party region if our standby region becomes unresponsive beyond the agreed RTO.

I'll loop in Sean (CS lead) and Laura (Legal) to finalize language. Can you confirm the exact maintenance window (start/end in UTC) and whether read-only fallback is an acceptable compensating control?

Regards,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Monica / team — quick internal note before we send formal language to Orchard. Summary/concerns:

- Operationally feasible: we can author a scoped amendment for a single-day maintenance window. We will need the migration start/end times and a runbook signature from Orchard.
- Risk: relaxing RTO to 4 hours means traffic queuing and potential token billing spikes if downstream apps retry aggressively. Recommend we add a mitigation clause requiring Orchard to enable backoff headers and a max-open-connections cap during the window.
- Fallback: routing to a third-party region incurs cross-cloud egress costs and possible data residency flags for EU customers — confirm region-specific exclusions.

Action items I propose:
1) Ask Orchard for explicit UTC window and a short operational runbook (30–60 minutes).
2) Draft a short SLA amendment (1 page) that includes rollback triggers and cost carveouts.
3) Laura to review wording around liability/credits.

I'll draft the amendment text and flag items for Legal. Markus, can you review the technical fallback language?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Eliot — appreciate the window and the confirmation. Attached is a first-draft one-page amendment and the updated failover design slides (redwood-failover-design-v2.pptx). Key points:

- Scope: Single maintenance window on Nov 15, 2028, 02:00–10:00 UTC.
- Temporary SLA: standby-region RTO <= 4 hours; RPO <= 2 hours. Applies only to workloads explicitly included in Appendix A.
- Mitigations required from Orchard: pre-migration checklist (signed), enable HTTP Retry-After/backoff headers, and accept read-only fallback for non-critical workflows.
- Cost/credit carveouts: If failover to third-party region occurs, extra egress charges will be invoiced to Orchard; Redwood will provide a cost estimate within 48 hours after event.
- Rollback/trigger: automated rollback if health checks fail for > 6 hours.

Laura — tagging you for legal language. Markus — please confirm the fallback paragraph (routing, KV cache reseed) is accurate. Sean — I'll propose the amendment for signature by Nov 6 to give Procurement time.

If this looks good I can route the DocuSign link by COB Monday.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
